name: Deadwater Protocol: The Underworld Has a Physical Address
description: Among Underworld navigators and deep-net divers, the Deadwater Protocol refers to the belief that the Underworld's most secure nodes are not merely distributed across server architecture — they are physically anchored beneath Lake Michigan in a decommissioned water treatment megastructure called Cistern Nine. The theory claims that Cistern Nine was purchased off municipal record by a consortium of E.L.F. collectives in 2198 and retrofitted as a cold-server vault, legally invisible because it predates GLMZ's incorporation boundary. Diver crews who've attempted to locate the physical coordinates report navigation anomalies and BCI interference consistent with active countermeasure fields.
cultural_impact: The myth has spawned a subculture of 'Cistern hunters' — divers and drones who probe the Lake Michigan substrate on weekends, some for profit, some out of genuine conviction. Legitimate salvage operations near the old treatment corridor have become contested and occasionally violent.
story_hooks: A salvage crew hired for a routine lake-bottom retrieval job finds infrastructure that matches no municipal blueprint — and something inside it is still drawing power.
Ysolde Mbuyi-Krantz goes silent after posting partial coordinates to a deep-net board; her last BCI ping places her 40 meters below the lake surface.
A player with a corporate salvage license is offered triple rate to map Zone 7 — and warned by a Shelf contact to refuse.
believers: Deep-net divers, Underworld brokers, E.L.F. rights advocates, Shelf salvagers
evidence: Cistern Nine is a real decommissioned structure whose ownership records are genuinely absent from public databases. BCI interference in Zone 7 has been independently reported but could have mundane explanations. No one has returned with visual confirmation of the interior.
